topic: Ecosystem mobile rendering and animation performance
currentUserGoal: Keep the ecosystem redesign visually busy while making the phone experience fast, smooth, and ready to scale toward a 100x100 field.
workCompleted: Profiled the actual ecosystem prototype at 390x844 instead of using the obsolete legacy tile harness.
Added projection-geometry change detection so routine production renders reuse stable viewport, tile, chunk, and grid geometry.
Stopped unchanged production ticks from rebuilding the field grid, repositioning every visible tile or chunk, relaying out helper actors, or reapplying identical texture keys.
Kept stage changes live by updating only tile or chunk textures whose resolved key actually changed.
Reduced the phone close-up animation budget from 72 to 48 representative tiles while leaving all visible tiles rendered.
Capped the phone single-plot ambient mote animation pool at 10 while preserving the full desktop presentation.
Added ecosystem harness counters for projection reuse, grid redraws, helper layout passes, texture changes, zoom, visible candidates, and ambient mote count.
Verified resize behavior and touch registration after moving between 390x844 and 1280x720.
verificationRun: npm run check passed: ESLint, 183 Vitest tests across 23 files, strict TypeScript, and the Vite production build.
Targeted animation-budget and viewport tests passed: 9 tests across 2 files.
Busy 100x100 phone far view with all eight helpers: 144 FPS, 0 frame spikes, 0.089 ms average frame work, 0.036 ms average animation work, and 0.025 ms average field-render work.

Busy 100x100 phone near view with all eight helpers: 110 rendered tile views, 48 animated representatives, 144 FPS, 0 frame spikes, 0.101 ms average frame work, 0.060 ms average animation work, and 0.033 ms average field-render work.
The 100x100 far view stayed bounded at 100 rendered chunk views; no full-field scans or per-frame production loops were reported.
Desktop 1280x720 resize verification retained all 100 chunk views and accepted the first field touch with 0.1 ms average input latency and 1.9 ms touch action work.
Phone and desktop screenshots showed intact field framing, chunk grids, HUD layout, helper actors, and Memory Grove presentation.
Browser diagnostics contained no warnings or errors, and git diff --check passed apart from normal Windows LF-to-CRLF notices.

gitStatus.expectedAfterCommit: Mobile performance pass committed locally; master is one commit ahead of origin/master and has not been pushed or redeployed.

knownIssues: The debug panel requires many repeated currency clicks to assemble a fully funded stress field; a dedicated one-click ecosystem stress-state control would make future profiling faster and more repeatable.
The current browser refresh ceiling was 144 FPS, so these measurements demonstrate ample main-thread headroom rather than real low-end-phone GPU performance.
Future visual systems must continue using pooled, viewport-bounded actors and representative effects instead of scaling display objects with all 10,000 logical tiles.
nextRecommendedSteps: Run a hands-on phone test on physical mid-range hardware when available, focusing on battery heat, touch latency, and sustained production.
Add a one-click ecosystem stress-state debug control before the next deep profiling pass.
Continue the early Growth and first-expansion pacing work once the user is satisfied with mobile feel.
Push master and deploy Vercel only when the user requests the next release.
doNotRevert: Do not resume unconditional field-grid clearing, helper relayout, or texture assignment on every dirty production render.
Do not increase phone animation counts without measuring the actual ecosystem route at phone size.
Do not use the legacy 1200-tile harness as evidence for ecosystem redesign performance.
Do not touch docs/CODEX_GITHUB_SETUP_GUIDE.md without explicit user direction.
